gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each under-$250 4K front-and-rear camera measured in a named tester's hands when both cameras record: Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K at 23.8 Mb/s on its 4K rear and 8.7 W driving (EricSan, DashCamTalk), Miofive S1 Ultra's 4K rear at 25 fps and later 24 fps rather than the manual's 30 (rcg530), and VIOFO A229 Pro 2CH parking draw of 4.50 to 4.98 W (rcg530).
standout_why: Compared against productbible.com (both pages), roadgearlab.com, the-gadgeteer.com, digitalcameraworld.com, knowledgelib.io and dashpicked.com; caranddriver.com and thecargearguide.com could not be opened. Both Product Bible pages and Dashpicked carry no reviewer measurement at all. The Gadgeteer has one (Vortex Radar: ROVE R2-4K Dual records 25 fps, not 30). Knowledgelib gives the Miofive's 30/25 fps without a clear source and GameRevolution's fps drop on the A810 Lite. RoadGearLab already has DashCamTalk bitrates for the A229 Pro (57 front / 25 rear Mbps) and the 70mai A810S (29 / 10 Mbps), so that part is not new. None has any measured parking-mode wattage, any measurement of a dual-4K camera's rear stream, the Miofive's parking-mode start delays, or the rear-camera temperature reading.
decides: It sharpens the pick rather than overturning it. Among true dual-4K cameras under $250, the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K (a partner-store product at $239.99, no record yet) is the one with a named measurement of 30 fps on both channels; the Miofive S1 Ultra's 4K rear measured 25 then 24 fps and took about 31 s to start recording in time-lapse parking mode. The catch is that the Vantrue's 4K rear got 23.8 Mb/s, about the same as the A229 Pro's 2K rear at 25 Mbps, so it spreads roughly the same data over 2.25 times the pixels. Parking draw does not separate the candidates: all measured about 4.1 to 5.0 W in recording parking modes, so any of them needs a hardwire kit with a voltage cutoff or a battery pack. No named measurement turned up for the DDPAI N5 Pro or Z90 Pro, so our linked rows cannot carry a measured figure. VIOFO's own store search listed the A229 Pro 2CH at $349.99 today, which puts it over budget at the maker; the $219.99 figure on Product Bible is an Amazon price dated 2026-11-19 that I did not re-read.
